state.projectTitle: Iron Triangle Tycoon: Balance Scope, Time & Cost (COM0463)
state.organisation: Istanbul Kültür University, Computer Engineering Dept.
state.targetPopulation: COM0463 IT Project Management students (3rd/4th year undergraduates, n≈40)
state.problemStatement: Students understand the iron triangle (scope/time/cost) theoretically but make systematic errors when asked to trade off constraints under pressure. A tycoon game creates a living, breathing project where all three constraints are simultaneously active and visibly interdependent — a scope increase makes the time meter spike and the cost bar turn red, instantly.

sixDim.what: 15 project scenarios (3 per COM0463 topic chapter); 3 resource dials (Scope 0–100%, Time 0–100 days, Cost $0–$500K); 8 constraint levers (Add Feature, Cut Feature, Add Resource, Remove Resource, Fast-Track, Crash Time, Defer Phase, Change Quality Standard); Random Event deck (15 events: client whims, vendor failures, team illness, regulatory changes); Project Health indicator; Client Satisfaction score; Board of Directors approval mechanics
sixDim.why: Flow: Scenario 1 = single constraint slider adjustment; Scenario 15 = simultaneous triple constraint crisis with random events. SDT Competence: correct lever combinations restore triangle balance; wrong ones cascade. MDA: Mechanics=lever pull; Dynamics=cascade discovery; Aesthetic=Challenge+Mastery.
sixDim.who: Achievers 40% (portfolio score, leaderboard), Explorers 35% (discover unusual lever combinations), Free Spirits 25% (find Pareto-optimal solutions)
sixDim.when: 5 scenarios per chapter block (3 chapter blocks over 12 weeks). Each scenario: 15–20 min.
sixDim.how: The triangle is visible at all times. Every lever pull immediately updates all three dials. Students cannot hide from the consequences of their decisions. Client Satisfaction score decreases if the triangle goes out of balance for >3 turns.
sixDim.where: Vanilla JS + SVG animated triangle, single-file browser app.

state.narrativeTheme: You're the PM of a tech startup. The client is watching every decision. The Board wants ROI. The triangle glows green when you're in control — and turns blazing red when you're not. One wrong lever pull and the whole project collapses.
state.narrativeArc: Rising Action: A project manager takes control of a complex IT project with three competing constraints — Cost, Time, and Scope — all demanding attention simultaneously. Every decision shifts the balance of the Iron Triangle. Early phases reveal how resource allocation affects downstream project health. The KPI dashboard turns abstract PM theory into visible real-time consequence. Climax: A multi-front Iron Triangle crisis strikes in the Execution phase — budget overrun, schedule slip, and scope creep arrive simultaneously, requiring integrated PMBOK change management decisions under maximum pressure. Falling Action: The project reaches its closing phase in better or worse shape depending on every prior decision. Resolution: Final project delivery report connects every tycoon management decision to the specific COM0463 constraint management principle it demonstrated.
state.characters:
Project Manager (Student): Acts as PM making decisions under Iron Triangle constraints facing stakeholder pressures and resource conflicts.
Stakeholder NPCs: Configurable characters representing client, sponsor, team member, and regulator with defined Power/Interest positions.
Game Master (Facilitator): Human instructor triggering event cards, adjusting parameters, guiding debrief connected to Marchewka theory.
state.storyWorld: The Iron Triangle Tycoon world is a fully simulated project environment where the classic PM constraint triad — Scope, Time, and Cost — are living, interactive forces that respond to every management decision. The project command centre dashboard shows all three KPIs in real time. Stakeholder demand events represent the sponsor, client, and regulator pulling the triangle in competing directions. Crisis events model the compounding consequences of ignored constraint violations — consequences that any COM0463 graduate must understand how to prevent and manage.

conceptMappings.mechanic: 3 dials (Scope/Time/Cost) permanently visible; all 3 update on every lever pull
conceptMappings.rationale: Real-time automatic interdependence calculation makes the theoretical triangle viscerally experienced — students feel the cascade before they understand it formulaically

conceptMappings.mechanic: Add Resource lever reduces time by allocating cost; Crash Time lever reduces time by spending budget exponentially
conceptMappings.dynamic: Add Resource: −5 days, +$20K. Crash Time: −3 days, +$60K. Students discover when each is appropriate.
conceptMappings.rationale: The non-linear cost of crashing vs linear cost of resourcing is the key PM principle — the tycoon game makes students discover it through experimentation, not lecture

conceptMappings.mechanic: Random Event deck periodically spawns "Client Whim" events demanding feature addition; student must accept, reject, or negotiate
conceptMappings.dynamic: Accept: triangle destabilises. Reject: client satisfaction −15%. Negotiate: requires 2-turn delay but preserves satisfaction.
conceptMappings.rationale: Every real project has uncontrolled external scope pressure — the random event deck simulates this and forces students to practise the accept/reject/negotiate decision under time pressure

mdaAnalysis.mechanics: Iron Triangle resource management (Cost/Time/Scope), Decision event system (PMBOK project scenarios), KPI dashboard (earned value metrics), Stakeholder demand events, Crisis response options, Team PM+Sponsor mode, Project delivery outcome leaderboard.
mdaAnalysis.dynamics: The competing KPI system creates genuine tension between Iron Triangle dimensions — improving scope performance often degrades cost performance, mirroring real project management trade-off dynamics. Stakeholder demand events inject realistic pressure for constraint renegotiation. Crisis response options require PMBOK change management knowledge to resolve without cascading KPI damage.
mdaAnalysis.aesthetics: Challenge (Iron Triangle management demands genuine PMBOK constraint knowledge), Strategy (long-horizon resource allocation mirrors real PM planning), Accomplishment (successful project delivery with all three KPIs in green creates genuine achievement), Submission (tycoon management perspective creates authentic engagement with COM0463 constraint trade-off dilemmas).

state.introText: You have just been appointed Project Manager of a complex IT delivery. The Iron Triangle is your responsibility: Cost, Time, and Scope must all be managed simultaneously — and they will fight each other for your attention. The KPI dashboard shows your project health in real time across all three constraint dimensions. Stakeholder demand events will push you to expand scope, compress schedule, and cut budget all at once. Use your COM0463 knowledge of earned value management, change control, and scope management to keep all three KPIs in the green and deliver the project successfully.

scenarios.name: Budget Crisis
scenarios.title: Iron Triangle Tycoon — Budget Crisis
scenarios.setup: Sprint 7, $80K over budget. Client satisfaction 61%. Deadline in 15 game-turns.
scenarios.objective: Restore triangle balance; reach project completion with satisfaction ≥75%
scenarios.winCondition: Project delivered with satisfaction ≥75%, cost within 5% of target
scenarios.loseCondition: Client satisfaction drops to 0, or cost exceeds target by >20%
scenarios.storyboard: Budget crisis alert → Lever selection → Triangle update → Random event (client demands new feature) → Lever adjustment → Turn 10 mid-point check → Delivery → Debrief
scenarios.outcome: Win (satisfaction ≥75%, cost ≤5% over): +300 + Portfolio Star. Partial (50–74%): +120. Fail: −40 + Mandatory debrief.

activities.action: Identify which lever to pull to reduce cost by $20K without increasing scope or time
activities.description: Budget crisis: $80K over. Student must select the correct lever (Cut Feature or Remove Resource) and justify the choice.
activities.trigger: Budget Crisis event activates at turn 1
activities.winCondition: Correct lever selected; cost reduces ≥$20K; triangle returns to amber (not green yet)
activities.loseCondition: Wrong lever selected (e.g. Crash Time costs more, worsening crisis)
activities.loseResult: Cost increases; triangle turns red; client satisfaction −10%
activities.neutralCondition: Correct lever but over-correction (cost drops >$40K, scope impact)

activities.action: Respond to a Client Whim event demanding a new feature mid-crisis
activities.description: Turn 6: Client Whim card — "Add analytics dashboard by next sprint." Student must choose: Accept, Reject, or Negotiate (2-turn delay).
activities.trigger: Client Whim event card drawn at turn 6
activities.winCondition: Negotiate selected; delay accepted; feature queued for Phase 2; satisfaction maintained
activities.winResult: +120 XP + Scope Guardian badge + satisfaction maintained at current level
activities.loseCondition: Accept selected; scope expands; triangle destabilises further
activities.loseResult: Triangle in red; −20 satisfaction; cascade event triggered next turn
activities.neutralCondition: Reject selected; feature not added; client satisfaction −10%

scenarios.name: Triple Crisis
scenarios.title: Iron Triangle Tycoon — Triple Constraint Crisis
scenarios.setup: All three constraints simultaneously out of balance: scope +20%, cost +15%, time −8 days.
scenarios.objective: Restore triangle to green within 5 turns
scenarios.winCondition: Triangle returns to green (all 3 constraints within target) within 5 turns
scenarios.storyboard: Triple alert → Emergency lever sequence → Random event complicates recovery → Satisfaction drops → Final lever combination → Triangle recovered → Portfolio update
scenarios.outcome: Recovery in 3 turns: +400 + Triple Crisis Master badge. 4–5 turns: +200. Failure: −50.

activities.action: Design a 3-lever sequence that restores all three constraints simultaneously
activities.description: Pull levers in optimal order: Cut Feature (reduces scope, cost, prevents time extension) → Remove Resource (reduces cost) → Fast-Track (uses budget to reduce time).
activities.winCondition: 3-lever sequence restores all constraints to green within 3 turns
activities.loseCondition: Sub-optimal sequence worsens at least 1 constraint

scoringSystem.bonuses: Triangle never turns red: +100. Client Whim Negotiated (not accepted): +60. All 15 scenarios: +200 portfolio completion bonus.
scoringSystem.penalties: Triangle stays red 3+ turns: −20/turn. Client satisfaction drops to 0: scenario ends with −100.
scoringSystem.badges: Portfolio Star, Cost Controller, Scope Guardian, Triple Crisis Master, Iron Triangle Champion (all green)

rewardTiers.elite: Iron Triangle Champion (all 15 scenarios, satisfaction ≥75%): 5-pt course bonus
rewardTiers.professional: Triple Crisis Master (all SC-02 scenarios recovered ≤5 turns): 3-pt bonus

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Conduct full platform test on target lab devices 24h before session. Prepare a paper-based fallback version of the PM tycoon game challenges. Verify browser compatibility on all student devices.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Switch to prepared paper-based fallback immediately. Instructor verbally presents COM0463 PM challenges; students answer on printed worksheets. Session data manually entered into system post-session.

tuslerRisks.risk: Widespread Rule Misunderstanding at Session Start
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Provide multi-modal game introduction: verbal briefing, printed rule card, and in-game tutorial overlay for the PM tycoon game. Conduct a 2-minute practice round before official scoring begins.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Facilitator pauses game immediately on detecting widespread confusion. Re-delivers rule explanation using a specific worked example. Q&A window opened before resuming. Game timer reset if necessary.

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Design PM tycoon game scoring to reward both performance and COM0463 PM concept demonstration. Integrate mandatory reflection checkpoints mid-session where students must explain their decision rationale.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor intervenes to redirect student focus to COM0463 PM learning objectives. Post-session assessment weights conceptual understanding over game performance score explicitly.

tuslerRisks.mitigation: Implement adaptive difficulty that reduces challenge intensity if a student is failing repeatedly in the PM tycoon game. Provide visible progress indicators so students always see incremental advancement.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Facilitator provides individual encouragement and targeted hint. Adaptive system reduces challenge difficulty for the next COM0463 PM task. Optional easier entry point offered without public announcement.

tuslerRisks.risk: Assessment Misalignment with Course Learning Outcomes
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Conduct formal COM0463 PM curriculum alignment review before deployment. Map every PM tycoon game challenge item to specific course learning outcome statements in the alignment matrix.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor conducts post-session targeted debrief correcting any COM0463 PM misconceptions surfaced by game challenge outcomes. Misaligned challenge items flagged for removal before next session.

tuslerRisks.risk: PMBOK Methodology Applied Incorrectly Through Game
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Conduct subject matter expert review of all PM tycoon game PMBOK challenge scenarios before deployment. Map every decision point to a specific Marchewka chapter and PMBOK process group.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor leads targeted post-session debrief correcting PMBOK misconceptions surfaced by PM tycoon game outcomes. Challenge items producing widespread incorrect PMBOK reasoning flagged for redesign.

tuslerRisks.risk: Students Fixate on Single KPI, Ignoring Triple Constraint Dynamics
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Implement KPI imbalance detection: if any single KPI is ignored for >3 consecutive decision events, the game triggers a Stakeholder Alert event forcing attention to the neglected constraint dimension.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor uses single-KPI fixation examples in post-session debrief as teachable moments about COM0463 integrated constraint management. Marchewka triple constraint chapter reference provided with specific fixation examples.

tuslerRisks.risk: Crisis Event Overwhelms Students Without Sufficient PMBOK Scaffolding
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Provide PMBOK decision scaffolding within crisis events: each crisis option displays its expected impact on all three KPI dimensions plus the relevant Marchewka chapter reference before the student must commit.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor pauses session during widespread crisis paralysis to deliver a brief PMBOK crisis response framework refresher using the active crisis event as the teaching example before students continue.

tuslerRisks.risk: Sponsor Role in Team Mode Creates Adversarial Rather Than Collaborative Dynamic
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Brief both PM and Sponsor role students on the collaborative intent of the team mode before session. Structure Sponsor demands as negotiation opportunities rather than constraints, with explicit compromise outcomes designed into the event system.
tuslerRisks.responsive: Facilitator intervenes if PM-Sponsor dynamic becomes genuinely adversarial. Brief paired debrief conducted to reset collaborative frame. Event severity reduced for the remainder of the session to allow relationship recovery.

conceptualMap.description: Three simultaneous KPI metrics directly operationalise the PMBOK triple constraint model — students experience how optimising one dimension always affects the other two.
Cost Performance Index and Schedule Performance Index KPIs directly implement PMBOK EVM metrics — students apply EVM diagnostic reasoning in a live consequence environment.
Decision events requiring trade-off choices between cost, time, and scope operationalise PMBOK integrated change control — changes must be evaluated across all constraint dimensions.
Stakeholder demand events model the PMBOK stakeholder management reality that scope expansion requests arrive continuously and must be managed without derailing the triple constraint.

Four game phases (Initiation/Planning/Execution/Closing) mirror the PMBOK process group sequence — each phase intensifies constraint management demands in alignment with Marchewka's project lifecycle model.
conceptualMap.courseReference: Marchewka Ch 2-5: Project Lifecycle and Process Groups

state.instructorRole: The instructor should only be assigned the role of questioning the game. No additional roles beyond questioning should be assigned. The instructor's focus is on facilitating reflection, probing understanding, and guiding critical thinking — not participating in game mechanics. If the instructor participates as a player, grading objectivity and the psychological safety of students may be compromised.
state.gameDurationRules: No single game should exceed 30 minutes of active gameplay. Total session including introduction and debrief: 30 minutes. Recommended timing: Introduction 5 min + Active gameplay 20 min + Debrief & reflection 5 min. Instructor may pause at any time for teaching moments. Games exceeding time limit are concluded at the current phase boundary.

gameDynamics.progressionSystems: Game structured in four project phases (Initiation, Planning, Execution, Closing), each with phase-specific Iron Triangle challenges. KPI thresholds tighten as the project advances. Project delivery outcome (On Time/On Budget/Full Scope) determines leaderboard tier and badge award.
gameDynamics.feedbackLoops: Real-time KPI dashboard provides continuous visual feedback on all three constraint dimensions. Decision event outcomes (crisis resolved/escalated) provide immediate consequence feedback. Phase transition report provides a structured feedback checkpoint. Final project delivery report provides comprehensive PM decision quality assessment.
gameDynamics.competition: Leaderboard by project delivery outcome tier (All Green / Two Green / One Green / Project Failed). Weekly Iron Triangle Master badge for achieving all three KPI targets in minimum decision events. Class-wide project outcome distribution is displayed post-session to stimulate discussion of PM strategy variety.
gameDynamics.collaboration: Team PM mode pairs students in PM role (controls Cost/Time) and Sponsor role (controls Scope demands and stakeholder events). Competing priorities must be negotiated through structured change request process, mirroring real PM-sponsor dynamics. Team project delivery outcome displayed on paired leaderboard.
gameDynamics.adaptability: KPI threshold values and decision event pool configurable by COM0463 topic focus. Phase duration adjustable for session length. Stakeholder demand event frequency and severity configurable per cohort level. Crisis event pool swappable to cover different PMBOK knowledge areas per session.

condition1.check: Has the player's enterprise achieved all three KPI targets within the round limit?
condition1.outcome: Game ends. Full XP and Business Architect badge awarded. Debrief commences.

condition2.check: Has the player's budget reached zero or a critical KPI dropped to red for 3 consecutive rounds?
condition2.outcome: Game ends. Partial XP for KPIs achieved. Instructor reviews decision analysis in debrief.

condition3.outcome: Game concludes at current round boundary. XP awarded for KPIs met. Full debrief commences.

state.sdtAutonomy: Students autonomously select which Iron Triangle constraint management approach to deploy against project management challenges without prescribed sequences. Different strategy combinations produce different project outcome scenarios, allowing exploration of PMBOK methodology trade-offs through self-directed experimentation aligned to COM0463 knowledge areas. Students control their own game pacing within the session timer.
state.sdtCompetence: Each correctly applied project management tool or decision in the tycoon management game delivers XP feedback tied to the PMBOK knowledge area addressed. The upgrade or mastery tree makes PM methodology progression explicitly visible, with advanced tools unlocking only after foundational PMBOK processes are demonstrated. Difficulty scaling within COM0463 topic areas ensures students are challenged at their developing frontier of PM understanding.
state.sdtRelatedness: Class-wide project outcome leaderboard after each session creates cohort-level comparison of PM decision quality. Optional team PM mode pairs students in complementary project roles, requiring joint PMBOK-based decisions. Post-session debriefs where students explain their PM strategy choices to the class create peer teaching moments grounded in COM0463 methodology and Marchewka frameworks.

state.deliverableJust: A browser-based tycoon/dashboard is uniquely suited because: (1) Active decision-making with immediate consequence creates stronger encoding than passive delivery; (2) Game mechanics directly parallel domain processes (see Concept-to-Game Mapping); (3) Performance logging enables objective Bloom L3+ skill assessment.
state.howEthics: Student participation is voluntary; equivalent written task available for opt-outs. All performance data anonymised in aggregate reports. Data collected under KVKK and GDPR, disclosed in course syllabus. Assessment based on participation and reflection, not competitive ranking. Instructor monitors emotional wellbeing; distress triggers private check-in.
state.platform: Browser-based web application; any modern browser. No installation required. Compatible with IKU computer labs, student devices, and mobile browsers.
state.narrativeEvolution:
Phase 1 — Initiation (KPI Baseline): The project begins with all three KPIs in green. First scope request arrives from the sponsor. Students make initial resource allocation decisions. Cost variance and schedule performance index begin tracking. COM0463 concept: project initiation, scope baseline, and Marchewka Chapter 6 cost and schedule integration.

Phase 2 — Planning Crisis: A scope change request arrives simultaneously with a budget constraint from the sponsor. The Iron Triangle tension becomes visible: accepting scope expands cost; compressing schedule to compensate risks quality. COM0463 concept: integrated change control, scope and schedule trade-offs, and Marchewka Chapter 10 risk integration.

Phase 3 — Execution Storm: Multiple KPIs enter amber simultaneously. Earned value metrics (CPI and SPI) provide diagnostic data for corrective action decisions. Crisis response options require selecting the correct PMBOK corrective action. COM0463 concept: earned value management, schedule control, and Marchewka Chapter 11 project monitoring.

Phase 4 — Closing Delivery: Final project delivery report generated. All-green delivery earns Iron Triangle Master badge. Partial delivery triggers gap analysis. Debrief connects every tycoon decision to COM0463 constraint management theory, Marchewka Chapters 6, 10, 11, and the triple constraint model.
state.lbCats: Participant Names | Total XP | Badges | Session Rank | Personal Points % = (player XP / total class XP) x 100 | Villager Win Rate | Vampire Win Rate
state.whyMotivation: Students are motivated through three SDT core drives: Autonomy — Iron Triangle tycoon management strategy selection without prescribed answers allows genuine PMBOK methodology reasoning rather than answer retrieval, transforming passive knowledge recall into active strategic decision-making. Competence — the progression structure aligned to PMBOK knowledge areas creates a transparent mastery ladder where PM understanding feels like tangible capability growth and not just test performance. Relatedness — class leaderboard and team PM mode connect individual PM knowledge to a shared project challenge narrative, reducing the isolation of individual PM problem-solving. Through the Octalysis lens, the dominant Core Drives are Development & Accomplishment (PM progression), Challenge (game events demand real PMBOK knowledge), Social Influence (class leaderboard and team mode), and Epic Meaning (protecting the project from failure).
state.personaList:
Persona 1 — The PM Methodologist: Deep PMBOK theory background. Approaches the tycoon game analytically, applying PMBOK process group sequencing to all decisions. Derives satisfaction from correct methodology application. May become frustrated if game mechanics do not accurately reflect PMBOK best practices.

Persona 2 — The Pragmatic Problem Solver: Moderate PM knowledge, prefers learning through practical project management decisions rather than theory. Discovers PMBOK principles through trial-and-error in the tycoon game. Risk: may develop misconceptions if incorrect decisions are not debriefed in post-session review.

Persona 3 — The Budget Optimizer: Focused on resource efficiency above all other project constraints. May underinvest in PM tools and be surprised by late-game scope creep or risk events. Needs instructor prompts to apply full PMBOK constraint management.
state.logPrivacy: Activity logs retained 6 months. Accessible only to facilitator and research team. Student identifiers anonymised in aggregate reports. Data per KVKK and GDPR. Students informed via course syllabus. Data destruction certificate at academic year end.
